summary:
Turn 7 opened the next Candidate on the accept-phase status responsibility, with the previous two reachability questions recorded as disposed.

With no open Candidate left and the map at audit spec v4, the product selects the premise carried forward from the last two turns: handleAccept stores Deps, Seq, bal and vbal for instance (Replica, Instance) and never writes inst.Status, so an accept quorum member that never saw the PreAccept holds accepted attributes with Status NONE, while one that did see it keeps PREACCEPTED/PREACCEPTED_EQ. Three places in the code are written as if an acceptor's acceptance were observable: handlePreAccept's >= ACCEPTED guard, which exists to avoid regressing accepted attributes; findPreAcceptConflicts' "already ACCEPTED or COMMITTED" shortcut; and handlePrepareReply's sub-case 2, which is defined by lb.status == ACCEPTED. The Candidate asks whether any decision depends on that status, specifically whether a later PreAccept can recompute and downgrade accepted attributes because the guard cannot fire, and whether a recovery that should re-accept an already accepted value instead falls to the phase-1 restart because the accept-only acceptor reports Status NONE.

Counterevidence is recorded with it: the leader-side accept branch does set ACCEPTED together with the merged attributes, so recovery sub-case 2 is reachable through a recovering replica's own record even though acceptors never report it; bcastPreAccept and bcastAccept draw peers from the same PreferredPeerOrder prefix, so an accept-only acceptor needs the alive set to change between the two broadcasts; and the findPreAcceptConflicts shortcut lives in the TryPreAccept path, which is already known to be unreachable dead code, so the omission cannot change that decision. The remaining unknowns fix the discriminators (same-ballot PreAccept reaching an accept-only acceptor; whether a command-less, status-NONE reply at the accepted vbal changes what the recovery re-proposes), and the supporting behaviours are named so the guards and recovery dispatch stay visible.

No map object was changed, so the map keeps its v4 basis and its B5 unknown describes the same premise at the level already recorded. No requirement, premise or previously explained result was weakened.
